title: Opportunities and constraints

blocks.heading: Opportunities and constraints
blocks.text: Global connections can expand markets, finance and knowledge while exposing producers to competition, shocks and unequal bargaining. Judge participation, local retention, capacity and environmental effects. An increased flow is not by itself proof of a net local benefit.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Opportunities
blocks.text: Access to larger markets, suitable investment and knowledge can support productive activity. Benefits require the ability to meet quality and delivery needs and opportunities for local workers or suppliers to participate.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Constraints
blocks.text: Infrastructure gaps, missing skills, finance barriers or dependence on dominant buyers can limit global participation. External competition can challenge local firms while widening consumer options; compare who gains and loses under the stated conditions.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Use the evidence
blocks.text: Explain which fictional global-production offer better fits retained local skills: A offers more output but imports all specialist staff; B offers less initially with local training and supplier links. B better fits the skill-retention aim if its programme works. A offers greater immediate volume, but output alone does not establish transferred capabilities or retained supplier gains; weigh those actual arrangements.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect to Industrialisation (4.1), Production (3.1) and investment/aid (9.2). Keep transaction type, time period, units and local development criteria explicit. The data is fictional.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
